title: Parabolic quotient torsor and rational lifting over any field
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth, affine of finite type and geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after extension to an algebraic closure. Unipotent means admitting a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation in which all geometric points are unipotent matrices. A parabolic $k$-subgroup $P\subseteq G$ means a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose fppf right-coset sheaf $G/P$ is represented by a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here the coset sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/P(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras, and $G(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)$. Let $P$ be such a parabolic and write $q:G\to G/P$ for the canonical quotient map. Left multiplication defines an action of $G$ on $G/P$, with $q(ag)=a\cdot q(g)$. The map $q$ is a right $P$-torsor: it is faithfully flat and finitely presented and $(g,p)\mapsto(g,gp)$ is an isomorphism $G\times_kP\xrightarrow{\sim}G\times_{G/P}G$. Consequently for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ one has $q_A^{-1}(q_A(1))=P(A)$. The map $q_k:G(k)\to(G/P)(k)$ is surjective. These assertions require neither infinitude nor perfectness of $k$.

source.place: Theorem 25.9(b), printed p.546; its proof handles finite k by Theorem 17.98 (Lang) and infinite k by local sections. Quotient/torsor construction: Theorem 5.28, Sections 5(g) and 8(a); the proof of 25.9(b) explicitly identifies fibres as P-torsors.

proof.text: Regard schemes as their representable algebraic spaces [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. The gluing theorem [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf], applied to coverings converted by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], makes their functors of points fppf sheaves. Put $Q=G/P$. Left multiplication preserves right-coset equivalence: $(ag)p=a(gp)$. Thus $(a,[g])\mapsto[ag]$ defines a presheaf action, and defines a sheaf action by locally choosing representatives and gluing; a replacement $g\mapsto gp$ leaves its image unchanged. The same identities prove the unit, associativity and $q(ag)=a\cdot q(g)$ on every test scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] with $L=P$. Its hypotheses hold: $G$ is affine and finite type; affineness gives separatedness since the diagonal is induced by the surjection $k[G]\otimes_k k[G]\to k[G]$. Obtain $p:G\to X$ flat, surjective and finitely presented, with $p(a)=p(b)$ exactly when $a^{-1}b\in P$. The inverse formulas $(g,h)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}h)$ and $(g,p)\mapsto(g,gp)$ give its kernel-pair isomorphism. Since $p$ is an fppf covering, all its pullbacks are coverings by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. Every test section of $X$ therefore lifts fppf locally. Two lifts differ exactly by $P$, so the sheaf axiom identifies $X$ with the fppf coset sheaf: locally lift to $G$, take its coset, and glue; the inverse sends local cosets to their common image under $p$. The maps are inverse after the covering, hence globally. This identifies $p$ with the specified $q$ and proves the asserted faithful flatness, finite presentation and torsor isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 5.24, Proposition 5.25, Corollary 5.27 and Theorem 5.28, pp.104--105; Stacks topologies.tex Tag 021O (lemma-fppf), part (3).

proof.text: For any commutative $k$-algebra $A$, apply the torsor isomorphism to the pair $(1,g)$. It lies in $G\times_QG$ exactly when $q_A(g)=q_A(1)$, and its unique preimage has the form $(1,p)$ with $p\in P(A)$. Therefore $g=p$. Conversely $q_A(p)=q_A(1)$ for every $p\in P(A)$ by right-coset invariance. This proves the kernel assertion on all algebras, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Lemma 5.24, p.104; evaluation of its isomorphism at (1,g).

proof.text: Choose a closed split torus $S\subseteq P$ of greatest rank. Here is the elementary existence check, so no conjugacy theorem is being assumed. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-dual-number-calculus], $T_1P$ is finite dimensional and a closed subgroup induces an injection on tangent spaces. For $\mathbf G_m^r$ the tangent vectors are the tuples $(1+\epsilon a_i)$, so their dimension is $r$; ranks of split tori in $P$ are therefore bounded by $\dim_kT_1P$, and rank zero occurs. A greatest-rank torus is maximal under inclusion: by [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices] an inclusion of equal-rank split tori is given by a square integer matrix. Since it is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], its Laurent-coordinate map is surjective; linear independence of Laurent monomials forces its exponent lattice map to be surjective. A surjective square integer matrix is invertible over $\mathbf Z$, so the inclusion is an isomorphism. Now [lem-sfb-parabolic-prescribed-split-cocharacter], applied to this $P,S$, gives a $k$-cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to S\subseteq G$ with $P=P_\lambda$ on every test algebra.

source.place: Theorem 25.1, converse, p.544; preparatory cocharacter choice in Theorem 25.6(b), p.546. The bounded-rank choice is expanded using tangent injections (10.14, p.190) and integer torus maps (12.9(a), pp.233--234).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-subgroups] over $R=k$ to $a(t,g)=\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$. The finite-presentation hypothesis on $G$ holds because smoothness is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], while an affine morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its subgroup $P_a$ is exactly $P$. Write $N=U_{-a}$. The cited statement gives an open immersion $m:N\times_kP\to G$, $(u,p)\mapsto up$. In particular its restriction with $p=1$ is the inclusion $N\to G$, and $1\in N(k)$. All constructions are over the original field.

source.place: Theorem 25.1, p.544; Theorem 13.33(d), pp.265--266, as used in Theorem 25.9(a), p.546. The existing relative dynamic-subgroup statement supplies the same open multiplication over k.

proof.text: The map $q|_N:N\to Q$ is a monomorphism: if $q(u)=q(v)$, the torsor formula gives a unique $p$ with $v=up$, and injectivity of the open immersion $m$ gives $(u,p)=(v,1)$. Moreover $N\times_QG\simeq N\times P$ by $(u,p)\mapsto(u,up)$, so its projection into $G$ is exactly the open immersion $m$. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-local-open-subfunctor-descent] to $h_N\to h_Q$ with local presentation $h_G\to h_Q$ supplied by step 1 and open $m(N\times P)\subseteq G$. The monomorphism and pullback hypotheses have just been verified on all tests. It follows that $q|_N$ identifies $N$ with an open subscheme $U\subseteq Q$. Its inverse, followed by $N\to G$, is a section $s:U\to G$ of $q$. Also $q(1)\in U(k)$.

source.place: Tag 02WU (lemma-finding-opens), descent of the cell open; explicit monomorphism and pullback calculations from Milne 13.33(d), followed by the local-section construction in 25.9(a), p.546.

proof.text: Suppose $k$ is infinite and fix $x\in Q(k)$. Let $V$ be the inverse image of $U$ under the $k$-morphism $G\to Q$, $g\mapsto g^{-1}\cdot x$. This is open and nonempty: a local lift $h$ of $x$ exists by step 1, and $h^{-1}\cdot x=q(1)\in U$, so $V$ has a point after an fppf covering of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply [lem-sfb-infinite-field-reductive-rational-density] to this nonempty open to choose $a\in V(k)$. Then $y=a^{-1}\cdot x\in U(k)$ and $g=a\,s(y)\in G(k)$ satisfy $q(g)=a\cdot q(s(y))=a\cdot y=x$. Density applies to the reductive $G$, without assuming the field perfect.

source.place: Theorem 25.9(a),(b), p.546, using Theorem 17.93(b), p.382. The rational-translate argument is written for each rational point, which suffices for (b).

proof.text: Suppose $k$ is finite and fix $x\in Q(k)$. Pull the fppf covering $q$ back along $x$. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change], the fibre $Y=\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{x,Q}G$ is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation over $k$. Right multiplication by $P$ preserves this fibre, and the base-changed isomorphism of step 1 is exactly $(y,p)\mapsto(y,yp):Y\times_kP\simeq Y\times_kY$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-sfb-finite-field-connected-group-torsor-point] hold with $H=P$, since the given parabolic is smooth, geometrically connected, affine and finite type (it is a closed subgroup of the affine finite-type $G$). Choose $y\in Y(k)$. Its projection is a $g\in G(k)$ with $q(g)=x$. The finite and infinite cases exhaust all fields, proving the final surjectivity assertion.
